'''Testament of John Glasgow'''  
*Died: May 1577  
*Parish: Irvine, Ayrshire  
*Testament type: Testament Testamentar and Inventory  
*Executor: William Glasgow, lawful son  

=== '''Original Transcription (Modernised Spelling)''' ===  
*The Testament Testamentar and Inventory of the goods, gear, sums of money, and debts pertaining to the late John Glasgow in the parish of Irvine at the time of his decease, who died in the month of May 1577...  
*Faithfully made and given up by William Glasgow, lawful son to the deceased and executor dative decerned to him...  
*Item, the said deceased had goods, gear, and furnishings of his body estimated to be worth...  
*And the said William, being sworn, made oath as executor that he knew of no other goods pertaining to the said deceased John Glasgow at the time of his death...

*Item, the said deceased was owed certain debts and sums of money as follows...  
*Item, there was owed by the said late John to the persons underwritten the following debts:  
**To Thomas Glasgow his son – 20 merks  
**To Jonet Glasgow his daughter – 10 merks  
**To Andrew Glasgow his son – 20 merks  
**To Margaret Glasgow his daughter – 10 merks

=== '''Confirmation Snippet (Andrew Glasgow)''' ===  
*The confirmation of the testament of Andrew Glasgow...

=== '''Inferred Family Table''' ===  
*'''John Glasgow''' – died May 1577 in Irvine  
**'''William Glasgow''' – son, executor of testament  
**'''Thomas Glasgow''' – son, owed 20 merks  
**'''Andrew Glasgow''' – son, owed 20 merks, later confirmed his own testament  
**'''Jonet Glasgow''' – daughter, owed 10 merks  
**'''Margaret Glasgow''' – daughter, owed 10 merks


=== Attempt 1 ===

''Testament of '''Johne Glasgw''', Irvine (d. 1577)'' 

== '''Original Transcription''' ==

''The testament testamentar and inventar of the guidis, geir, sowmes of money and dettis pertaining to umquhile Johne Glasgw in Irvine the tyme of his deceis, quha deceisit in the moneth of Aprile the yeir of God 1577 yeris...''

''Faithfullie maid and gevin up be Katherine Mure, his relict and onlie executrix testamentar...''

''Item, thair wes awand to the said umquhile Johne be William Glasgw his brother german...''

''Item, be Alexander Glasgw, merchant burges of Irvine...''

''Item, be Thomas Glasgw...''

''Item, be Johnne Huntar, sone lawfull to James Huntar in Knokintibbert...''

''Item, be Johnne Andersone, elder in Bigtoun...''

''Item, be James Mure, brother to the said Katherine...''

''The said testament wes confirmet at Edinburgh the ferd day of Maii the yeir of God jM⁵⁷⁷ yeris...''

''The confirmatioun of ye testament of Andro Glasgw burges of Irwyne quha deceist in the moneth of Julii 1576 faythfullie maid and gevin up be himself and nominat his spous as his executrix testamentar… with power to intromit with his guidis and geir and to dispone thairupon as executrix lawfullie decernit be the commissar of Edinburgh the xxvj day of Aprile the yeir of God 1577.''

== '''Modern Translation''' ==

This is the testament and inventory of the goods, possessions, sums of money, and debts belonging to the late '''Johne Glasgw''', of Irvine, who died in '''April 1577'''. His testament was faithfully made and submitted by his widow and sole executrix, '''Katherine Mure'''.

At the time of his death, the following individuals owed him money:

* '''William Glasgw''', his brother
* '''Alexander Glasgw''', merchant and burgess of Irvine
* '''Thomas Glasgw''', likely a close relative
* '''Johnne Huntar''', lawful son of '''James Huntar''' in '''Knockintibbert'''
* '''Johnne Andersone''', elder in '''Bigtoun'''
* '''James Mure''', Katherine’s brother

The will was confirmed by the Edinburgh Commissary Court on '''4 May 1577'''.

The record also includes confirmation of the testament of '''Andro Glasgw''', burgess of Irvine, who died in '''July 1576'''. He made his own testament and nominated his '''wife''' (unnamed) as executrix. This was confirmed on '''26 April 1577'''.

== '''Inferred / Estimated Family Table''' ==

* '''Johne Glasgw''' — deceased in April 1577, of Irvine  
* '''Katherine Mure''' — wife and sole executrix  
* '''William Glasgw''' — brother  
* '''Alexander Glasgw''' — merchant, burgess of Irvine; likely relative  
* '''Thomas Glasgw''' — likely relative (possibly another brother or cousin)  
* '''James Mure''' — Katherine’s brother  
* '''Andro Glasgw''' — possibly Johne’s brother or cousin, deceased July 1576  
* ''Unnamed wife of Andro'' — executrix of his testament  
* '''James Huntar''' — of Knockintibbert; debtor  
* '''Johnne Huntar''' — his son; debtor  
* '''Johnne Andersone''' — elder of Bigtoun; debtor  

== '''Final Notes & Analysis''' ==

* All evidence points to the Glasgw family being established in Irvine with multiple members conducting business and trade (e.g., Alexander as a merchant).
* The presence of multiple Glasgws in the same document, including Andro and three debtors with the surname, suggests a kinship network active in Ayrshire commerce.
* The relationship between Johne and Andro is not explicitly stated but strongly implied by timing, geography, and proximity in court records.
* The Mure family also appears to be locally rooted and well-connected, with James Mure named.
* The record does not mention children of Johne or Andro.
